svg.title: A month after the PHP and Node.js fixes of 21 October 2026: Node.js downloads beside Python downloads, and PHP services counted from outside
svg.desc: Two line charts, one above the other, each with its own unit, by day since the releases of 21 October 2026 (day 0) to day 30, 20 November. The top chart is downloads: the share of each fixed Node.js line's daily downloads from nodejs.org that were the fixed release or newer. On day 7 line 22 was at 53.9%, line 24 at 72.2% and line 26 at 64.7%. On day 30, counting three newer versions first seen on 11 November (day 21) as fixed, a rule chosen after the counts were seen, they were 65.5%, 74.3% and 96.3%; thinner lines from day 20 show the rule as first written, which leaves those versions out and ends at 39.8%, 60.6% and 85.8%. Behind them, a band shows the range of four Python security fixes' share of their library's daily downloads, 55.6 to 59.5 per cent on day 7 and 57.3 to 72.3 per cent on day 30, and a dashed line the median over 37 Python libraries, 61.6% on day 30; those releases date from April to August 2026. The bottom chart is services seen from outside: the share of internet-facing PHP services reporting a version in each fixed branch that Censys counts as patched. On day 7: 8.2 53.0%, 8.3 52.4%, 8.4 67.8%, 8.5 78.8%; on day 14: 8.2 73.4%, 8.3 70.4%, 8.4 81.0%, 8.5 89.7%; on day 30: 8.2 78.2%, 8.3 75.0%, 8.4 86.5%, 8.5 92.2%. A dashed line marks half in each chart. Downloads are requests, not machines; Censys's patched shares are floors, because distributions that backport a fix keep the old version number and a service counts only after a rescan; after day 14 three PHP branches' shares rose mostly because fewer services were counted in them. Sources: nodejs.org download summaries and Censys ARC's PHP2Shell dashboard, read by Lighthouse to 22 and 21 November 2026; ClickPy's copy of the Python Package Index download log, read 28 September 2026.
svg.text: A month after the fixes of 21 October 2026
Two kinds of count, drawn apart: requests to download servers, and services seen from outside.
Each panel has its own unit. Day 0 is the release day (UTC), a part day; day 30 is 20 November.
Downloads: share of a day's downloads at the fixed release or newer
Node.js (nodejs.org) and Python (PyPI): requests in a day, not machines
11 Nov: three newer Node.js versions appear

svg.text: Node.js: thick lines count three versions first seen on 11 November as fixed, a rule chosen after the counts were seen;
thin grey lines, from day 20, leave them out, as first written. Python: four security fixes and 37 libraries, April to August 2026.
PHP: after day 14, three branches rose mostly because fewer services were counted in them, not more patched.
Sources: nodejs.org summaries (read to 22 Nov 2026); Censys ARC PHP2Shell (21 Nov 2026); ClickPy (28 Sept 2026).
